newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha rallies on crudes, physical demand.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha rallies on crudes, physical demand.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices soared in afternoon Tokyo trade on Friday, buoyed by healthy regional fundamentals as well as sharp gains in crude oil, traders said.
"Naphtha levels shot up due to firmer crudes, but brisk demand for physical cargoes added to the strength," one trader said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half February was assessed at $226.00/227.00. It was traded at $221.75 in late trading on Thursday.
Second-half January was quoted at $229.00/230.00, compared with Thursday's $223.50/224.00.
Although the market has firm buyers, offer levels are mostly notional with sellers holding back for further naphtha gains, traders said.

In middle distillates, kerosene prices firmed towards the winter, with levels indicated at $1.80 to $1.90 above the mean of Singapore quotes on a cost and freight (C and F) basis, compared to $1.50 to $1.70 premiums earlier this week.
Japan's kerosene stocks as of the end of October totalled 4.95 million kilolitres, down 0.8 percent from a year earlier. Inventory level were within market expectations, traders said.
